canada.title: N.L. gas tax will be re-assessed every three months following changes to legislation
canada.summary: Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly is working through a bill that will allow a cut to the provincial gas tax as of Dec. 1. But the government and Opposition are at odds over changes in the bill that will set up a regular review of the tax cut going forward.

canada.title: Wildfire at Base Gagetown continues for 2nd day
canada.summary: A wildfire has burned 25 hectares at Base Gagetown due to an artillery shooting Wednesday afternoon.

canada.title: Apparent arson attack outside home of Sikh independence activist prompts police investigation
canada.summary: The Sikhs For Justice group says the attack occurred at the home of Narinder Singh Randhawa, who was given a "duty to warn" notice by Surrey police in April and told there was an imminent threat to his life.

canada.title: ‘Highly contagious’ disease that only affects rabbits, hares, confirmed in N.W.T.
canada.summary: Northwest Territories government officials say rabbit hemorrhagic disease virus (RHDV) has for the first time been confirmed in dead snowshoe hares found in the territory. The disease poses no risk to humans but can be fatal in rabbits and hares.

canada.title: Inquest into death of Regis Korchinski-Paquet on hold for investigation: coroner
canada.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Toronto woman who fell from a 24th-floor balcony while police were in her home was put on hold indefinitely Thursday just as it reached the final stretch of the proceedings.

canada.title: Experts highlight the 'double-edged nature' of Starlink in the North
canada.summary: Starlink became part of daily life in Nunavut, but it also changed community life in Nunavut. Now, the federal government is looking for made-in-Canada alternatives to the technology.

canada.title: Alberta referendum saw 70.4% turnout — highest voter participation in decades
canada.summary: The turnout is the highest for a provincewide vote since at least 1975, but it fell short of breaking the record of 81.8 per cent turnout seen in the 1935 general election.

canada.title: Critics renew concern over Quebec data centre project as U.S. developer cancels open house
canada.summary: A U.S.-backed developer planning a data centre project in Sherbrooke, Que., abruptly cancelled a public open house this week — prompting more criticism from skeptical residents demanding transparency.

canada.title: N.S. university teachers association says premier is using political intimidation
canada.summary: The Association of Nova Scotia University Teachers says it condemns the premier’s response, calling it a threat to academic freedom.

canada.title: Tumbler Ridge shooting survivor Maya Gebala being released from hospital, father says
canada.summary: A 13-year-old girl who was severely injured in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting is being released from hospital after nearly nine months of uncertain recovery, her father says.

canada.title: We’re losing the war on rats. What if there was a different way?
canada.summary: Rats are resourceful, resilient and “here to stay,” veterinary pathologist and epidemiologist Chelsea Himsworth says. She leads the Vancouver Rat Project

canada.title: School support staff union, province heading back to bargaining table
canada.summary: CUPE says it wants school support workers to get at least $3.50 more per hour over four years. On Thursday afternoon, the union said it received indication from the province that the government is willing to resume bargaining.

canada.title: Montreal police explain day-long delay in dismantling unit accused of misconduct
canada.summary: A 16-member patrol unit remained armed and active for nearly a full day after investigations secured enough evidence to take action against officers accused of criminal misconduct.

canada.title: Ottawa quietly abandoned its promise to end thermal coal exports, auditor finds
canada.summary: A report from the federal auditor general published Thursday reveals Environment and Climate Change Canada quietly gave up on its plans to end thermal coal exports years ago without notifying the public and without record of being directed a do so.

canada.title: Officer shot in Belleville synagogue attack released from hospital
canada.summary: Police in Belleville say an officer who was shot on Yom Kippur while protecting a synagogue full of worshippers from an armed attacker has been released from the hospital.

canada.title: High-risk sex offender released, expected to live in Winnipeg
canada.summary: Convicted sex offender Douglas Wayne Bowman, 62, has been released after a lengthy prison sentence, and Winnipeg police are warning the public he is considered a high risk to reoffend.

canada.title: Fire at New Brunswick military base not threat to public: defence officials
canada.summary: The Department of National Defence says the blaze in the northeastern part of the Canadian Forces Base Gagetown training area is being monitored.

canada.title: 'It feels fantastic,' Scott Gillingham says after winning another term as Winnipeg mayor
canada.summary: After winning his second consecutive term as Winnipeg mayor, Scott Gillingham says the city's best days are still to come. He had 39.8 per cent of the ballots cast, with all polls reporting just before 10 p.m. Wednesday.

Aiden Pleterski’s lavish ‘Crypto King’ persona drew in scores of investors, Toronto Star reports.

Maya Gebala, who survived the horrific mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, has been released from hospital—262 days after she was airlifted to B.C, The Canadian Press reports.

Elke Sommer, the striking blonde bombshell of German descent who was a mainstay of 1960s Hollywood comedies and espionage movies including “The Prize” and “A Shot in the Dark,” has died, The Associated Press reports.
